clue.text: Spend less by cutting noble gent's tithe

indicators.note: cutting up the words noble gent's tithe chops them so their letters can be rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words, apostrophe ignored, are the raw material

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted aristocrat economises by trimming the tithe he pays to the church.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in gent's is ignored; all fifteen letters of the three words are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to economise, as if pulling in your belt because you are eating less.

clue.text: Overweight comedian Eddie creates storm

parts.note: read as over plus weight: lb, the pound abbreviation, turned over in this down clue
Eddie Izzard is a British stand-up comedian

explanation.surface: A heavy comic causes a commotion on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Overweight looks like a description of the comedian, but it splits into a reversal signal and the word weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe snowstorm with high winds is a specific kind of storm.

clue.text: Movement comprises Unionist Irishmen

indicators.note: the phrase Unionist Irishmen comprises, or contains within it, the letters needed

parts.note: the answer runs across the join, unioniST IRishmen

explanation.surface: A political movement is made up of Irishmen loyal to the Union.
explanation.definitionFit: A stir is a slight movement or a commotion, as in not a stir in the house.

clue.text: Rod's machine makes pub seating

parts.note: a rod is a bar, and the apostrophe s is kept
a tool is a device or machine for doing work

explanation.surface: Someone called Rod has a machine that turns out seats for pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod looks like a man's name, but it is a metal bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall stool at a counter is a typical seat for drinkers in a pub.

clue.text: Glance back, then increase and maintain speed

indicators.note: back asks for the word for a glance to be written in reverse

parts.note: a peek is a quick glance
up as a verb means to raise or increase

explanation.surface: A driver checks the mirror, then accelerates and holds the pace.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to stay level with others, matching their pace.

clue.text: Outdated CID can't kick the habit

parts.note: read as out plus dated: out tells us to rearrange, and dated is the fodder
taken as written; the Criminal Investigation Department

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned detective department is unable to break its bad ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Outdated must be split into Out, the anagram signal, and dated, part of the fodder; CID is Britain's plain-clothes detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being hooked on something means you are unable to give up the habit.

clue.text: Throw a trial lasso

indicators.note: to throw the letters is to scatter them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cowboy has a practice cast with a rope.
explanation.walkthrough: Throw looks like the action of casting the rope; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A long rope with a running noose used for catching animals; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Great Bard modelled in stone inspires writer

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the stone takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: marble is a stone used by sculptors

indicators.note: modelled suggests clay shaped into a new form, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written, nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A marble bust of Shakespeare gives a writer her inspiration.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspires reads as encouraging the writer, but it means breathing in: the stone splits around the rearranged letters. The novelist wrote The Millstone.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a British novelist and biographer, so an example of a writer.

clue.text: Awkward having one student on Dead Sea trip

parts.note: L is for learner, as on a learner driver's plate
the late so-and-so is someone who has died

indicators.note: trip suggests a stumble that knocks the letters of Sea out of order

parts.note: taken as written, three letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A lone student feels uncomfortable on a holiday to the Dead Sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Dead Sea looks like one place name, but the two words are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Being uneasy or uncomfortable is a close synonym for feeling awkward.

clue.text: Play lead man in RADA production

indicators.note: a production makes something new out of the letters
the lead of a word is its first letter

parts.note: only the first letter of man is used
taken as written, the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art

explanation.surface: A leading man appears in a staging at the famous drama school.
explanation.walkthrough: RADA is the Royal Academy of Dramatic Art in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is a piece of theatre, which is a work of the stage.

clue.text: Risks are high on Arizona main routes

parts.note: A roads, written A RDS, are Britain's main roads

explanation.surface: Dangers are great on the highways of Arizona.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the main roads are numbered as A roads, such as the A1.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazards and risks are both dangers that might cause harm.

clue.text: Preparation for painting formal home requires glaze initially

parts.note: prim means stiffly formal and proper
in means at home

indicators.note: initially picks out the first letter of glaze

parts.note: only the first letter of glaze is used

explanation.surface: Decorating a smart house begins with a coat of glaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Priming is the first undercoat applied to a surface before painting.

clue.text: Made new cheese

indicators.note: new signals that the letters of made are formed into something fresh

parts.note: taken as written, four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A newly produced cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A mild Dutch cheese with a red wax coat, an example of a cheese.

clue.text: Rival company obtains permit to develop

indicators.note: to develop the letters is to grow them into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A competing firm secures planning permission to build.
explanation.walkthrough: To looks like part of to develop, but it belongs with permit as fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor is someone competing against you, a synonym of rival.

clue.text: Upset bald old crackpot

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A bald old eccentric is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an eccentric person with odd ideas or behaviour.

clue.text: It's not normal for Katy to lose head over photo by Pacino

indicators.note: losing its head means the name Katy drops its first letter

parts.note: the girl's name, taken as written before its first letter goes
pic is short for picture
Al Pacino is an American film actor

explanation.surface: Katy has her head stuck over a picture of the actor Pacino.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over places the pieces one above the other, so they follow in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Atypical means not typical, not representative of the usual type.

clue.text: Heard greeting suspect at sanctuary

indicators.note: heard says the two words are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: hi is an informal greeting and to doubt someone is to suspect them, so the pair is hi doubt

explanation.surface: Someone overhears a suspicious hello at a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: Said quickly, hi and doubt run together into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideout is a hiding place or refuge, a place of safety like a sanctuary.

clue.text: Call sailors to join line dance

parts.note: ho is a call to attract attention, as in land ho
RN is the Royal Navy
a pipe is a line carrying gas or water, as in pipeline

explanation.surface: Sailors are summoned to take part in a line dance.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Certainly disorientated when Fahrenheit was dropped!

indicators.note: was dropped tells us one Fahrenheit letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: being off course is being lost or disoriented

explanation.surface: A navigator was sure to get lost once the temperature fell.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropped looks like falling temperature; it is the removal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an emphatic yes, meaning naturally or definitely.

clue.text: All over for always when unknown girl comes between us

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns

indicators.note: comes between means the girl is placed inside the word for us

parts.note: we is the subject form of us
her is a pronoun for a girl

explanation.surface: A romance ends for good when a mysterious woman splits a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: All over means in every place, as in spilled all over the floor.

clue.text: Bonuses for people in films

definitions.meaning: first meaning: additional things given on top of what is expected
second meaning: actors hired for crowd scenes with no speaking part

explanation.walkthrough: The link word for joins two meanings that read like film-set perks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both added bonus items and the background actors in a crowd scene.

clue.text: It's that man again in "High Noon", the killer

indicators.note: in puts the radio show inside the film's initial letters

parts.note: the initials of the western film High Noon
ITMA was a popular BBC radio comedy of the 1940s, known by its initials

explanation.surface: The villain returns in the western High Noon.
explanation.walkthrough: The film title gives only its initials, a convention the solver must spot unaided; ITMA was a 1940s BBC radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A hitman is a hired assassin, so a professional killer.

clue.text: Almost frighten Mark

indicators.note: almost means the word is not quite complete, so its last letter goes

parts.note: to scare is to frighten

explanation.surface: Someone nearly scares a man named Mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Mark looks like a name, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: Little girl eats chocolate bar with biscuit in the middle

indicators.note: eats means the short name swallows the chocolate bar

parts.note: Bet is a pet short form of Elizabeth, so a little version of a girl's name
a Twix is a chocolate bar with a biscuit centre

explanation.surface: A small girl munches a chocolate biscuit bar with a filling.
explanation.walkthrough: In the middle reads as the bar's filling but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic word means between, placed in the middle of two things.

clue.text: Worry salesman over beginning of recession in Bath

indicators.note: over asks for the salesman word to be turned over and read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: in places that first letter inside the bath

parts.note: a tub is a bathtub

indicators.note: beginning of picks out the first letter of recession

parts.note: only the first letter of recession is used

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman frets about the downturn in the city of Bath.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath looks like the English spa city, but it is just a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to disturb or worry them.

clue.text: Wander around ruins of Roma

indicators.note: the ruins of the word Roma are its letters knocked into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written, the Italian name for Rome

explanation.surface: A tourist strolls among the ancient ruins of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: To roam is to travel aimlessly from place to place.

clue.text: Fix up a climbing plant

indicators.note: up asks for the word for fix to be read in reverse

parts.note: to nail something is to fix it in place
taken as written, the article stays as it is

explanation.surface: Attach a creeper to a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: Fix up looks like a phrase meaning repair, but up is the reversal signal, and a simply follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A liana is a woody vine of tropical forests that climbs up trees.

clue.text: Outrage surrounds salary increase curtailed by work review

indicators.note: surrounds means the outrage word wraps round the pay rise

parts.note: to appal someone is to outrage them

indicators.note: curtailed means docked of its tail, the last letter

parts.note: a raise is an increase in pay

explanation.surface: Staff are outraged when a cut pay rise comes with a performance review.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is a formal assessment of an employee's performance at work.
